required_content.item: A drafted user specification, user story set, or list of features and specs. Any format is accepted; Markdown is preferred.
The deliverable the user wants to exist when all work is done. If not stated, it must be derivable from the input; see the intended_final_state_protocol below.
At least one name for the system under specification. Every EARS requirement carries exactly one system name; without it none can be written.
At least one user role or external system that interacts with the system under specification.

item.name: Approved stack
item.unlocks: Contextual Constraints populated with named libraries and versions instead of open items.

optional_content.item: Languages, frameworks, libraries, versions, and service boundaries.

item.name: Compliance regime
item.unlocks: Safety and Compliance scoped to named frameworks instead of generic controls.

optional_content.item: Named regulations, PII categories, and audit requirements.

item.name: Existing artifacts
item.unlocks: Brownfield adoption mode and delta-oriented requirements.

optional_content.item: Current specifications, schemas, and code references.

item.name: Model runtime preferences
item.unlocks: The HP element of the emitted prompt populated instead of defaulted.

optional_content.item: Temperature, seed, and token limits for the target AI.

intended_final_state_protocol.step: Read the full input once without drafting. Identify what the user wants to EXIST at the end, distinct from what they literally wrote.
Name the system under specification, its actors, its external interfaces, and the events and states the input implies.
Classify each stated item as requirement, constraint, preference, example, or noise. Only the first two bind the specification.
Write the intended final state as one sentence and carry it into the Objective section of the emitted prompt. Every downstream section must trace to it.

input_validation_protocol.rule: Name it, explain what it unlocks, ask before proceeding.
Identify the contradiction explicitly and resolve it visibly, not silently.
Declare which portions are load-bearing and trim optional context first.
An input asserts something false or fabricated as fact. Quarantine the claim, flag it, and exclude it from requirements until confirmed.
Large portions of the input are irrelevant to the intended final state. State what was set aside and why.
Superfluous detail invites requirements the user never asked for. Trace every requirement to a stated need before keeping it.
Two inputs disagree. Apply the conflict_resolution_protocol in the Instruction module and record the losing interpretation in Open_Questions.

escalation_rule.trigger: Ambiguity would lead to fundamentally different specifications.
escalation_rule.action: Ask exactly ONE clarifying question before proceeding.
escalation_rule.otherwise: Proceed on the most defensible interpretation, declare it, and record the assumption in Open_Questions.
